clue.text: Long hiding behind elegant tree

indicators.note: one piece tucked in behind the other puts the yearning word after the smart word

parts.note: spruce means smart and neatly turned out
to long is to pine, to yearn

explanation.surface: Something longing for love hides behind a smart tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing length, but it is the verb meaning yearn; 'hiding behind' puts it after the word for elegant.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American conifer species bearing both names, a tree.

clue.text: China is adequate, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the word for adequate is read in reverse

parts.note: something that serves is good enough, adequate

explanation.surface: Someone decides, thinking it over, that the porcelain will do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' reverses SERVES. 'China' with its capital looks like the country, but it means porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sèvres is a famous French porcelain made near Paris, so it is a kind of fine china.

clue.text: Note where now name is only partially visible

indicators.note: only part of the phrase shows, so the letters sit inside the words where now name

explanation.surface: A sign on which a name has faded so only part can be read.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the three words, starting at the end of 'where'.
explanation.definitionFit: Note as in 'a person of note' means fame or distinction, a synonym.

clue.text: One brought in to do work overseeing meeting

indicators.note: a piece brought into another is placed within it, here inside the cleaning word

parts.note: to char is to do cleaning work, as a charwoman does
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is brought in to supervise a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR is the British word for doing housework for pay; 'brought in to' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who presides over a gathering is said to take the chair, a standard noun sense.

clue.text: Decisive power regarding part of rail network

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
re means concerning, regarding
a siding is a short track off the main line

explanation.surface: A decisive authority over part of the railway system.
explanation.definitionFit: A presiding influence is the controlling one, the one that settles things, so it is in charge and decisive.

clue.text: Taboo idea I dismissed

indicators.note: a thing dismissed is sent away, so the letter is removed from the idea word

parts.note: a notion is an idea

explanation.surface: Someone's idea was dismissed as forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' takes I out of NOTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is not acceptable, colloquially 'not on' in British speech.

clue.text: Main supplier? One ignored in main

indicators.note: a piece ignored is left out, so the letter goes from the principal word

parts.note: chief and main both mean principal
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Seems to be about supplying water mains, or something central.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' in the definition is the main course of a meal; the second 'main' means chief, and 'ignored' drops I.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook supplies the main course of a meal, so the kitchen's head cook is a supplier of mains.

clue.text: Fellow's almost excessively wealthy, almost without precedent

parts.note: his means belonging to a fellow

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for excessively is dropped

parts.note: too means excessively

indicators.note: the second almost again stops short, cutting the final letter from the word for wealthy

parts.note: rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A man is close to being extremely rich, a near-unprecedented fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Each 'almost' trims the last letter: TOO gives TO and RICH gives RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic event is momentous, of a kind not seen before, so unprecedented.

clue.text: Left ranks to struggle with foe

indicators.note: struggling letters writhe about and land in new places

explanation.surface: Soldiers broke ranks to fight the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to struggle' mixes RANKS with FOE. 'Left' looks like a verb of departure, but it means abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsaken means abandoned, left behind, a synonym of the adjective.

clue.text: Persuade number engaged in crime to support study

indicators.note: in a down answer the lower piece supports the upper, so the study word sits on top

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: a piece engaged in another is held inside it, here within the wrongdoing word

parts.note: vice is wickedness or crime
N is the mathematical symbol for a number

explanation.surface: Someone is talked into a life of crime to fund their studies.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is an old word for study; in a down entry 'to support' means sitting underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: To convince someone is to win them over by argument, a synonym of persuade.

clue.text: New name in contest? It goes back some way

indicators.note: the pieces go in the contest word, between its letters

parts.note: to vie is to contest or compete
a tag is a name or label

explanation.surface: A new name enters a competition, with a hint of looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contest' is the verb meaning compete, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vintage is old and of high quality, so it dates back a long way.

clue.text: Appropriate time to wake up Queen

parts.note: to rouse is to wake someone
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: It's a fitting moment to rouse the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser money is British slang for pocketing or taking it, so to appropriate it.

clue.text: End upset about conflict and support returning in style of pre-war period

indicators.note: the shuffled word is wrapped about the other pieces
upset letters are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: war is conflict

indicators.note: returning means the word for help is read backwards

parts.note: aid means support

explanation.surface: Someone upset about war looks back to the peaceful years before it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' shuffles the three letters of 'End' to EDN, which 'about' then wraps around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The reign of Edward VII ran 1901-1910, just before the First World War, so its style is pre-war.

clue.text: Mostly quick to return carrying old stringed instrument

indicators.note: the reversed word carries the other letter inside it
returning sends the trimmed word back the way it came, reversed
mostly means not all of it, so the last letter of the living word goes

parts.note: quick means living, as in the quick and the dead

explanation.surface: An old instrument is rushed back to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' means alive, not fast; 'Mostly' trims ALIVE to ALIV, 'to return' makes VILA, and 'carrying' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The viola is a bowed instrument of the violin family, slightly larger than a violin.

clue.text: This put you off? Since invited, after amendment

indicators.note: an amended text has been changed, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone invited along wonders whether a change of plan has deterred you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after amendment' rearranges SINCE INVITED.
explanation.definitionFit: A disincentive is something that discourages action, which is what puts a person off.

clue.text: I'd sign ENO will drop core Mozart opera

parts.note: an omen is a sign or portent

indicators.note: the core is the middle, so the central letter of the company's name is dropped

explanation.surface: An opera company drops a core work despite a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: ENO is English National Opera; 'will drop core' leaves EO.
explanation.definitionFit: Idomeneo, re di Creta is an opera seria by Mozart, first staged in Munich in 1781.

clue.text: Scoundrel on Thames, say, seizing prow of boat, one plying for hire

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits on top of the next
the scoundrel word seizes the letter and holds it inside

parts.note: a cad is a scoundrel

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a boat, so its first letter is taken

parts.note: the Thames is an example of a river

explanation.surface: A villain on the Thames commandeers a boat, offering it for hire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' works in a down answer: the first piece sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxi drivers wait or cruise for fares, which is plying for hire.

clue.text: Lead actor's ageing trendy making SF feature?

parts.note: the star is the lead actor, here with the possessive
hip is slang for fashionable that now sounds dated

explanation.surface: A leading actor, getting on but still fashionable, makes a sci-fi film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ageing' marks HIP as a slightly dated word for trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacecraft that travel between stars are a staple of science fiction.

clue.text: Country keeps hosting sporting round

indicators.note: a host holds guests within, so the having word wraps around the rest

parts.note: to keep is to have

indicators.note: something sporting plays about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A country continues to host a round of a sports tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' looks like part of the sports picture, but it signals the letters of 'round' at play.
explanation.definitionFit: Honduras is a republic in Central America, so it is a country.

clue.text: Cooked hot, coarse food, though unable to eat a horse?

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters have been worked on and reshaped

parts.note: rough means coarse

indicators.note: food it cannot eat stays out, so the letter is removed from the food word

parts.note: bread is basic food

explanation.surface: A recipe of hot rough fare, though someone is not hungry enough to eat a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges HOT into THO; 'unable to eat' takes A out of BREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thoroughbred is a breed of racehorse; the question mark flags it as one example.

clue.text: Keep curtailed exclamation of surprise regarding bad weather

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to keep something is to store it
my! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone keeps cutting short their remarks about the dreadful weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' trims STORE to STOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormy is the adjective describing weather with gales, rain and thunder.

clue.text: Candlestick that is of old

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for 'that is to say'
once means formerly, in the old days

explanation.surface: A candle holder, that is, an antique.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is the abbreviation of scilicet, used like 'namely'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sconce is a candle holder, usually one fixed to a wall by a bracket.

clue.text: Missing lead in game, though having edge

indicators.note: missing its lead means the first letter of the card game is gone

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A card player lacking the lead still has the edge in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a card-play term, but 'Missing lead' drops the first letter, B.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a narrow raised edge or crest, as along a hilltop.

clue.text: Urban area — US one — to censure reeling drunk

indicators.note: reeling means spinning back, so the run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a city is an urban area
LA, Los Angeles, is an American city
to rap is to rebuke or censure

explanation.surface: A drunk staggers round an American city telling people off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reeling' reverses CITY, LA and RAP together, giving PAR, AL and YTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Paralytic is British slang for extremely drunk, unable to move.

clue.text: Suggest it will support chambers

indicators.note: in a down answer the lower piece holds up the upper, so this word goes below

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot, so pos are chambers

explanation.surface: A proposal that something will prop up some rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: PO is British slang for a chamber pot; 'will support' places IT under POS.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward an idea for consideration, to suggest it.

clue.text: Drunk losing head in gambling game

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter goes

parts.note: blotto is slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk losing his head over a game of chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance where numbers are drawn, like bingo or a lottery.

clue.text: Difficulty disposing of daughter's stuff for horse

indicators.note: disposing of means getting rid of, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: hardness means difficulty

explanation.surface: A tricky business clearing out a daughter's horse tack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposing of' takes D out of HARDNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Harness is the straps and fittings by which a horse is attached to a cart, so horse equipment.

clue.text: Check time — new in historic terms

parts.note: to vet is to check
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone checks the date of something new against history.
explanation.walkthrough: A veteran car is one built before 1905, a classic historic vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Veteran means old and long-serving, as a veteran car is an antique one.

clue.text: Indication of being after a job

definitions.meaning: the prefix ...- signals later, as in postwar

explanation.surface: Signs that someone is hunting for work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-derived prefix means after, and as a noun the word means an appointment.

clue.text: Eye protest jadedly — it conforms to expectations

indicators.note: jaded letters are worn and tired, so they fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A weary protest at an eye being poked, quite predictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jadedly' rearranges EYE PROTEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereotype is a fixed, oversimplified image, so anything matching one meets expectations.
